statuses.meaning: The requested control step completed and required proof is present.
Policy or required evidence forbids continuation.
One user decision or clarification can safely resolve the turn.
A provider or capability is not verified or cannot serve the request.
A packet, transition, receipt, or candidate violates its contract.
An unexpected provider or internal failure occurred without a valid domain result.

failure_policies.fail_closed: Required for security-sensitive, authorization-required, source_only, owner-locked, and proof-required paths when required evidence is absent or invalid.
failure_policies.ask_user: Used only when one bounded user choice or clarification can safely continue.
failure_policies.degrade_safely: Allowed for ordinary conversation when a nonessential host capability is unavailable and no unsupported claim is made.
failure_policies.unavailable: Used when a real host or continuity service is required but not verified. Prompt text never substitutes for the service.

invariants: PASS never proves a host side effect without its provider receipt.
BLOCK and INVALID do not permit fallback success prose.
ASK does not execute the candidate action.
UNAVAILABLE does not become ERROR merely because a capability is absent.
Ordinary conversation does not fail closed for an unused optional capability.

A pre-ingress authorization ASK becomes resumable only after evidenced host-session binding succeeds; Validation and Egress then emits exactly one ASK TerminalPacket under the originating SecurityDecision.

If required host-session binding is UNAVAILABLE, the proposed pending interaction remains inactive and Validation and Egress emits exactly one safe UNAVAILABLE TerminalPacket under the originating SecurityDecision with owner security_restraint; no ControlDecision exists and SecurityDecision remains ASK.
ASK and provider-caused pre-ingress UNAVAILABLE are mutually exclusive terminal outcomes of the binding attempt and never produce two TerminalPackets in one host turn.
Expired, exhausted, cancelled, replayed, or unbound authorization requests fail closed and do not silently create a fresh request.
